title: fast
description: FAST (FMRIB's Automated Segmentation Tool) segments a 3D image of the brain into different tissue types (Grey Matter, White Matter, CSF, etc.), whilst also correcting for spatial intensity variations (also known as bias field or RF inhomogeneities). The underlying method is based on a hidden Markov random field model and an associated Expectation-Maximization algorithm. The whole process is fully automated and can also produce a bias field-corrected input image and a probabilistic and/or partial volume tissue segmentation. It is robust and reliable, compared to most finite mixture model-based methods, which are sensitive to noise.

bias_iters.description: number of main-loop iterations during bias-field removal; default=4
bias_iters.title: Bias iters

bias_lowpass.description: bias field smoothing extent (FWHM) in mm; default=20
bias_lowpass.title: Bias lowpass

init_seg_smooth.description: initial segmentation spatial smoothness (during bias field estimation); default=0.02
init_seg_smooth.title: Init seg smooth

segments.description: outputs a separate binary image for each tissue type
segments.title: Segments

init_transform.description: initialise using priors; you must supply a FLIRT transform
init_transform.title: Init transform

other_priors.description: Alternative prior images (requires 3 files: prior1 prior2 prior3).
other_priors.title: Other priors

iters_afterbias.description: number of main-loop iterations after bias-field removal; default=4
iters_afterbias.title: Iters afterbias

in_files.description: Image, or multi-channel set of images, to be segmented.
in_files.title: In files
